correctness.rationale: For T SPD and W symmetric indefinite, direct multiplication of the specified two-factor P_{alpha,gamma} produces n zero error eigenvalues and the n real generalized eigenvalues of (alpha I-WT^{-1}W,T+alpha I); this block calculation was independently checked on a noncommuting instance at five gamma values. The Rayleigh quotient has strictly positive alpha derivative because T+WT^{-1}W is SPD; compactness yields uniform strict increase of BOTH extrema, including eigenvalue multiplicities. At alpha down to zero the extrema are nonpositive with a strictly negative minimum; as alpha tends to infinity both approach 1. The sum crosses zero once, making max(-ell_min,ell_max) strictly decrease then strictly increase; the extremal balance is the unique global minimum. The upper extreme is always <1 and the lower >-1 exactly when 2alpha>lambda_max(WT^{-1}W-T); no claim that alpha=0 is admissible. For n=2, vanishing trace in a T eigenbasis yields the stated positive quadratic root and explains b12 independence. Numerical recomputation (noncommuting T=diag(1,4), W=[[-2,1],[1,3]]) supports the exact formula but is not an infinite proof.
